title: Detecting divisibility in uniquely divisible $\mathfrak{N}$-semigroups via homomorphisms to $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$
summary: An $\mathfrak{N}$-semigroup is an archimedean, idempotent-free, cancellative and commutative semigroup. For example, the additive semigroup $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is a $\mathfrak{N}$-semigroup. Hewitt-Zuckerman showed that every $\mathfrak{N}$-semigroup admits a semigroup homomorphism to $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. We show that every uniquely divisible $\mathfrak{N}$-semigroup $S$ admits enough semigroup homomorphisms to $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ to detect divisibility in $S$. %They were studied by Tamura and Kobayashi.
